decisive_moments.reason: Pro directly addressed the strongest accessibility objection by distinguishing prominence from technical presentation and giving a concise plain-language example that includes the estimate, range, and replication limits.
Pro clarified that merely making caveats available is insufficient under headline-driven attention, while preserving accessibility through translated explanations and evidence-quality labels.

Con correctly identified model dependence, false precision, and comprehension as real risks, but did not establish why layered communication requires uncertainty to be less prominent rather than prominently explained.

flags.quote: If audiences cannot interpret intervals, foregrounding them may reduce uptake without improving judgment.
